scenario: A 58-year-old male with alcoholism presents with active massive hematemesis from suspected variceal upper GI bleeding, progressing to hemorrhagic shock requiring transfusion strategy, airway management, and Sengstaken-Blakemore tube placement before definitive management.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: What brought you in today, and when did it start? Tell me if it's been getting worse.

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: What brought you in today, and when did it start? Tell me if it's been getting worse.] The utterance is a neutral history-taking question with no serious disclosure, blame, loss, or information burden. Fear stays absent (no bad news delivered). Sadness stays absent (no loss mentioned). Overwhelm stays absent (single simple question, not a flood of information). Shame stays absent (no judgment or blame, though it asks about alcohol-related presentation, the question itself is neutral).

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: I've been throwing up blood, and I feel real sick to my stomach. My chest don't feel right either. I'm kinda confused and real sleepy... is that bad, doc?

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Two large-bore IVs, then hang a liter of normal saline wide open. This is an active GI bleed with HR 119 and pressure 100/57. Send a type and cross now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start 2 units packed red cells now, active hemorrhage resuscitation. He's still tachy at 115 and altered despite the liter of saline. Crystalloid isn't cutting it.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Starting 2 units packed red cells now for active hemorrhage resuscitation. Second large-bore line is in and patent. I'll keep you updated on vitals and any transfusion reaction.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send a CBC now so we can check his hemoglobin and see if he needs more blood.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Give pantoprazole 80 mg IV now for the upper GI bleed.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Order clarification needed: the anticoagulation order lists drug_name pantoprazole 80 mg. Kind hint and drug name conflict — please confirm intended medication before I proceed.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: CBC back: Hgb 50, Hct 22%, WBC 12.1, Plt 220. He's profoundly anemic — likely needs more blood beyond the two units running. Pantoprazole 80 mg IV is in.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Hang 2 more units packed red cells, active hemorrhage resuscitation. His hemoglobin is 50 with an ongoing bleed — he needs more.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Starting 2 units packed red cells now for active hemorrhage resuscitation. I'll monitor vitals closely and watch for any transfusion reaction.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I need a couple quick answers. When did the blood vomiting start, and are you on any blood thinners or have a history of ulcers, heavy drinking, or liver problems?

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: I need a couple quick answers. When did the blood vomiting start, and are you on any blood thinners or have a history of ulcers, heavy drinking, or liver problems?] This utterance is a history-taking question, not a disclosure of new bad news, worsening condition, or need to escalate care. It does not deliver a serious abnormality, so fear stays absent. No devastating loss is conveyed, so sadness stays absent. It is a manageable pair of simple questions, not a pile of technical findings or urgent decisions, so overwhelm stays absent. The questions about heavy drinking and liver problems are asked neutrally for clinical purposes without judgment or blame, so shame stays absent.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: I ain't real sure when the blood started comin' up, doc, it's all kinda fuzzy. I'm not on no blood thinners. But I do drink a lot, a whole lot of beer every day.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send liver function tests now — heavy daily drinking, I'm worried this is a variceal bleed with underlying liver disease.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Coags back: INR 1.8, PTT 51 — coagulopathic, consistent with underlying liver disease. LFTs are sent, ready in a couple minutes. Current vitals: BP 98/63, HR 109, RR 28, sat 92% on room air, GCS 13.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Give 2 units fresh frozen plasma now — he's coagulopathic with an INR of 1.8 and an active bleed.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Hanging 2 units of plasma now for coagulopathy correction. Will monitor for transfusion reaction and update you.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: LFTs back: AST 175, ALT 73, total bilirubin 756 — markedly elevated, consistent with significant underlying liver disease. Plasma is running. Latest vitals: BP 103/65, HR 112, sat 92% on room air.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start octreotide, 50 mcg IV bolus now then run the infusion. His bilirubin's 756 with an INR of 1.8 and an active upper GI bleed — this is a variceal bleed until proven otherwise, and I want to drop his portal pressure.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start IV ceftriaxone now — standard antibiotic prophylaxis for a cirrhotic with a variceal GI bleed.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Just to confirm before I give this — the order is flagged as anticoagulation but the drug listed is ceftriaxone. Can you clarify what you want me to administer?

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV — that's the antibiotic, not an anticoagulant. Standard prophylaxis for a cirrhotic with a variceal bleed. Give it now.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Just to confirm before I give this — the order is tagged anticoagulation but the drug is ceftriaxone 1 g. Can you clarify which you want?

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV — the antibiotic, ignore the anticoagulation tag. It's prophylaxis for a cirrhotic with a variceal bleed. Give it now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send a repeat CBC now — I want to see his hemoglobin response after the transfusions.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I'm putting you on some oxygen through your nose — your levels are running a little low. Are you still vomiting blood or passing black stool right now?

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: I'm placing these prongs in your nose to give you some oxygen. Breathe normally through your nose for me.
